message.content: The sea typically looks blue—especially when it’s clear and calm—because water absorbs colors at the red end of the spectrum and scatters blue wavelengths more efficiently. However, its appearance can change depending on depth, weather, time of day, and surrounding conditions; you might see greenish hues near shorelines, turquoise in tropical waters, or even grayish tones during storms.
